It's been 2 years since i completed this game and it still to this day manages to make me reminisce about that transcendent journey to the Edo era Japan and is the reason why I am making this review for those who felt put off from the game like I used to.

First while the plot synopsis seemed interesting, the artstyle put me off from playing this for years.
Then some time later I was struggling to find interesting translated visual novels to enjoy and so, searched for my favourite trope in VNDB tags and Chusingura was near the top of the results, just below Steins;Gate and ML Alternative.
I immediately bought it and boy what a ride it was. No regrets whatsoever even when it felt pricey for what it looked ought to be.

The artstyle i got over (and actually kinda started liking it) within hour or two. The wonky animations for fight scenes are luckily very scarce and didn't affect my opinion on this game at all.

All the small details in the game world (other than the genderswitch/play) felt so real. Like this was working world, characters had their roles to fill and lifelike prejudices against the MainChara all of that and much more felt so thought out.

I feel like that if the developers wouldn't have made this with eroge in mind, this might have been very well known staple of VN literature. It still is in my opinion, but it hides it well behind that artstyle.

This… wow… Okay, this takes the tale of the 47 Ronin and twists it in so many ways. You play as Suguha, who gets sent 300 years into the past. And he is sent to the Ako domain. The Ako being the Lord whose tragic dishonor is the impetus to all that follows. Well, not completely in Suguha’s case, but still… Anyway, there are five HUGE chapters, the first being free-to-play. Frankly, this took nearly a week to read through.

Through this read, you will experience the ups and downs of Suguha and the Ako Ronin. Note: four of the five chapters have Suguha falling in love with a different of the 46 Ronin (I think only one of which is male). And once the hidden conspiracy is fully revealed… well, he might have a bit of a choice on his hands as to who to end up with…

Fully recommend this title. Well worth the cost of Chapters 2-5…

----单线剧情视觉小说类游戏，以元禄赤穗事件为主线骨架，主角不断轮回，拯救别人的同时被拯救的故事。有第二部和“额外？”作品。
----文本量很大，每篇都花费了我至少八小时的时间[spoiler]也可能是因为我日语水平不高，外加喜欢百度所以比较慢[/spoiler]。除主角外全角色语音。
----因为是STEAM版，所以玩起来会觉得阉割得很暴力。黄油的部分不谈，和其他同类相比，Ctrl无法快进，前一幕的CG快进情况下会残留到下一幕[spoiler]存档后重开即可解决[/spoiler]，查看文本后右键不能返回，每过一段前一部分的文本就无法查看。另外，战斗描绘很敷衍。
----剧情方面，基本一篇一条线。第一篇是ご城代线，专享两种形态，一上来就攻略这个角色，主角真是厉害，提高了用剑水平，还学会了几乎吃遍全场的剑技。第二篇是安兵衛，这次是赤穗最强剑士，剑的LV再次UP。第三篇是主税，ご城代的女儿，开局好感度MAX，大概是拯救相信主角最多的角色。结果中间杀出个新八，看到选项我差点以为可以走新八线[spoiler]然后被切了，这个病娇真可怕[/spoiler]，百度了一下，第二部新开了新八线，从时间线来看这个才是真女主，不过我没玩过不知道。第四篇，勉强算是一魅[spoiler]也就是一学[/spoiler]线，同为穿越之人[spoiler]虽然一个是主动一个是被动，目的也不一样[/spoiler]，吉良后人，大概最强剑士，最终决斗的登场很帅。文本多是对历史和当局的解释、考证及推理，就像是急着想在下一篇完结一样[spoiler]事实也是如此[/spoiler]。第五篇，右衛門七线，存在感甚至不如妹妹，还被开了后宫，剧情走向和脑洞莫名，拉了个路人成BOSS，结局主角还成了内匠头的弟弟，各种大怪，输出靠吼，一刀带走。
----BGM方面，OP、ED和最终ED好评，尤其是那首“終わりの始まり”，总会让人想起那个石刻的相合伞。
----总的来讲是不错的作品，不过这游戏好像没打过折，所以推荐只买前三篇，即本体加第一个DLC。

[h1]One of the best Visual Novels on Steam [Period][/h1]

[b]Ultimately, ChuSingura46+1 is a trap.[/b] At first the game appears to be all boobs and action, however, that's a trick to get you into playing an emotional and powerful story loosely based on real historical events that becomes massively addicting. In fact, besides how quickly addicting the game becomes, it's surprising how historically accurate the game is. Besides an obvious gender swap and the other fictional aspects of the story, the events and backstories of the characters provide a great and entertaining insight into the real story of the 47 Ronin who avenged their master. It does it so well, it is  arguably better than any other modern English retelling (maybe even Japanese too)! So enjoyable, before I knew it, I was 30 hours in and 3 chapters completed in one weekend.

[b]If you haven't played ChuSingura46+1 S, do it.[/b] You won't regret your time playing. The first chapter is free and will provide you with an exciting, fun, and almost completely standalone fictional retelling of the events of the 47 Ronin. However, be prepared, it's hard to resist purchasing the following chapters based on how great the game is and wanting to hear more about its wide cast of characters.

[b]If like me, you get completely hooked playing ChuSinGura46+1 S, I promise you that you won't regret buying chapters 2+3 and 4+5.[/b] I purchased them at full price and have not regretted it for a moment. The story only continues to get better, Yasubee (the best character obvs.) gets a chapter heavily focused on her (thank goodness) and most importantly, the game stays fun and does not drag out like other longer visual novel. SO STOP READING THIS (IF YOU EVEN BOTHERED) AND PLAY CHUSINGURA46+1 NOW!

There is a clear love in the game from the developers, and the idea of getting a bit more in depth with the whole legend compared to the old western movie is greatly done.  The music is moving in just the right times, the sound effects are dead on about what happens.

The females are all 20 year old depictions, but are actually all well, forty with kids... Also, they have a tendency to change between "adult", to "7 year old kid" haphazardly, without any logic behind it.

And to top it off, as an european, I simply have a freakishly hard time with the whole...difficulty with saying stuff like: we have a feud, or I like you, and then suddenly, they change it to overaffectionate, since they need to "spice" up things a little more, for the game...

In the end, it is a slightly fun visual novel, which does not do it's job at getting you excited about the other 4 parts that the story is rich in any way.
